objections.claim: E6 still does not provide a deterministic discriminator. Exhaustively enumerating the finite mutation and conforming-input domains makes input coverage deterministic, but the candidate explicitly leaves kernel entropy and clock access available to the oracle. A RANDOM-EXIT oracle therefore has a nonzero probability of producing the required exit for every finite invocation; exhaustive inputs do not exhaust its entropy outcomes, so the assertion that it “fails some element ... deterministically” is false. Likewise, concealing a content-derived execution order does not convert nondeterministic oracle behavior into a deterministic verdict. This leaves an oracle that does not inspect the governed invariant capable of authorizing by chance, violating the frozen fail-closed requirement and deterministic-gate boundary. The authoritative mechanism must either eliminate/control every nondeterministic observation available to the oracle or use a deterministic validator whose correctness does not depend on finite black-box testing of arbitrary executable behavior; randomized or exhaustive mutation batteries may remain supplemental evidence.
